Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be dated in September 2025, but there's also Example 5 with dates in January 2025. Let me focus on the September 2025 examples first as they seem to form a consistent pattern.

## Analysis of Example 1 (2025-09-23)

History: Prices have been slowly rising from the low 70s to the mid-70s range
- Last 18 days: [71.72, 72.99, 73.97, 73.61, 74.95, 75.44, 76.04, 77.17, 76.90, 77.10, 75.54, 75.77, 76.75, 77.51, 76.98, 77.84, 77.55, 76.21]

Model forecast at day 1: 76.59
True outcome at day 1: 76.79

Model forecast at day 10: 78.41
True outcome at day 10: 78.75

Model forecast at day 20: 79.50
True outcome at day 20: 79.58

Looking at the pattern more carefully:

Let me compare model vs true for Example 1:
Day  | Model    | True     | Diff
-----|----------|----------|------
1    | 76.59    | 76.79    | -0.20 (model underestimates)
5    | 76.77    | 76.79    | -0.02 (almost correct)
10   | 78.41    | 78.75    | -0.34 (model underestimates)
15   | 78.43    | 78.12    | +0.31 (model overestimates)
20   | 79.50    | 79.58    | -0.08 (underestimates)


25   | 74.86    | 78.67    | -3.81 (model massively underestimates!)
